report.source_text: Pathology from the upper endoscopy revealed rare gland abscesses and diffuse lamina propria neutrophilic inflammation. Rare eosinophils were found as well as small lymphoid aggregates of polymorphic small lymphocytes. Stains for CMV and H. pylori were negative (after having received about two weeks of H. pylori directed treatment). There was no evidence of lymphoma or other malignancy.

report.source_text: The patient received a 14-day course of IV daptomycin (due to a medication reaction, IV vancomycin was deferred) and cefepime. He also eventually completed a two-week course of quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection. He was followed closely by Infectious Disease, General Surgery, and Gastroenterology during his stay. Half-way through the antibiotic course for phlegmonous gastritis his symptoms began improving, his appetite returned, and radiographic thickening of the gastric lining resolved. Three months following his initial hospitalization he is now in his usual state of health and follow up upper endoscopy revealed normal gross appearance of his stomach and esophagus. He did not require gastrectomy nor other surgical management.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Features overall were consistent with a diagnosis of phlegmonous gastritis and duodenitis.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old man presented with three weeks of severe epigastric pain, vomiting, and weight loss, after prior treatment for H. pylori gastritis. Initial upper endoscopy revealed congested, erythematous, eroded, friable, nodular, and scalloped gastric mucosa, and erythematous duodenal changes. Biopsies showed rare gland abscesses and diffuse lamina propria neutrophilic inflammation, with negative stains for CMV, H. pylori, lymphoma, or malignancy. An abdominal CT scan revealed diffuse bowel wall thickening of the stomach with mucosal enhancement, focal thickening with retained fluid, and diffuse adenopathy. Gastric biopsy cultures grew Granulicatella adiacens and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus. The patient was treated with IV daptomycin and cefepime, and later H. pylori quadruple therapy. Symptoms improved halfway through the antibiotic course, radiographic thickening resolved, and a follow-up endoscopy showed normal gross appearance. The patient returned to his usual state of health without requiring surgery.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with severe epigastric pain, vomiting, and weight loss, with prior H. pylori treatment.
Upper endoscopy revealed severe inflammation of the gastric and duodenal mucosa, including congestion, erythema, erosion, friability, nodularity, and scalloping.
Biopsies showed histopathological evidence of severe inflammation with rare gland abscesses and diffuse lamina propria neutrophilic inflammation.
Abdominal CT scan demonstrated diffuse bowel wall thickening of the stomach with mucosal enhancement and focal thickening, indicating transmural involvement.
Gastric biopsy cultures identified bacterial growth, including Granulicatella adiacens and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus.
Patient's symptoms improved and radiographic findings resolved with antibiotic treatment.
Follow-up endoscopy showed normal gross appearance of the stomach and esophagus.

Biopsies showed no evidence of lymphoma or other malignancy (E005).
